sentences.text: ORDER Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents.

2. The petitioner in this case is seeking a restraint order against the respondents to the effect that the respondents should not demolish the Idgah & Muslim Grave Yard (Sunni) situated in Sy.No.368 of Hudgi village, Taluk:
Humnabad, District: Bidar.
3. The extent of land is said to be 1 acre 36 guntas.
This claim is based on the premise that the land in question referred above was declared as the Wakf property vide notification dated 17.02.1974.
The records placed before this Court would indicate that the first respondent-National Highway authority has proceeded with the construction of National Highway connecting Hyderabad and Mumbai.

The records would also indicate that the highway between Hyderabad and Mumbai around the disputed property is completed, however the service road which is sought to be constructed in the disputed land is not completed because of the pendency of the writ petition.

4. Sri.Liyaqat fareed Ustad, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the mandate under Section 91(1) of the Wakf Act, 1995 (for short 'the Act of 1995) is not followed, as such the entire land acquisition proceeding is vitiated.
Under these circumstances, he would submit that the writ petition has to be allowed and the respondents should be restrained from utilising the land referred above.

5. Learned counsel Sri.Sreenath.V.K., appearing for first respondent would submit that the award is already passed on 11.09.2013 to the extent of the structure in Sy.No.368 referred above and it is further submitted that 2428 square meters out of 1 acre 36 guntas of land is to be utilised for the purpose of formation of service road and since the award is passed in respect of the structure the petitioner cannot claim any right over the property.
6.

It is stated that the award is produced before this Court on 09.02.2015 by serving the copy of the award to the petitioner and the petitioner did not avail the right to object the award under Section 91(4) of the Act of 1995.

sentences.text: This Court has considered the contentions raised at the bar and also perused the records.

8. The notification at Annexure-R2 would indicate that the property bearing Sy.No.368 referred above is a notified land under the provisions of the Act of 1995 and land is notified to be Wakf property.
In that event, there cannot be any dispute over the fact that the petitioner owned the property referred above.
For this reason the award is also passed in respect of the structure on the land.
9. The next question is whether the award passed by the first respondent-Authority should be treated as null and void for non-compliance of requirement of Section 91(1) of the Act of 1995.

No doubt, that the Wakf Act 91(1) of the Act, 1995 would prescribe the procedure relating to the acquisition of property belonging to Wakf and notice has to be given to the Wakf Board before acquiring the property under the provisions of land Acquisition Act of 1894, or any other law governing acquisition of land for the time being in force.
Admittedly, this procedure is not followed.
However, not following the procedure by itself would not render the award passed by the land acquisition officer, void.
The effect of the award is to be considered under Section 91(4) of the Act of 1995.

Under Section 91(4) of the Act of 1995, within one month of knowing about the order under Section 31 and 32 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, or any other corresponding law, if the objection is filed, then the order under Section 31 and 32 or any other corresponding provision under any enactment for acquisition of land will be declared as null and void.
10. In this case, the award is passed under National Highways Act 1956.
However the payment is not yet made.
No deposit is made under Section 3H of the National Highways Act 1956.

If the objection is filed within one month of coming to know about the deposit, then order relating to payment under Section 34 of the Act of 1956 will be rendered void and the award does not become void.
The party aggrieved will be entitled to raise his grievance relating to quantum of compensation.
11. In this case, the award is produced before this Court on 19.02.2015.
Till today the petitioner has not questioned the said award.
The records would reveal that the highway is already constructed.
The land in dispute is required for service road abutting the highway.
The service road on either side of land in dispute is also constructed.

By considering the overall materials before this court, this court is of the view that the restraint order prayed in the petition does not serve the larger public purpose behind the acquisition of the petitioner's property.
The private interest must yield to the larger public interest.
12. The petitioner though served with the copy of the award in the year 2015 itself, has not chosen to question the same.

Thus, the only legal option to the petitioner is to question the order under Section 3 H of the National Highways Act of 1956, by invoking Section 91(4) of the Act of 1995 within one month, of knowing about the order.
13. Under these Circumstances, this Court has to take a view that the award passed in respect of the structures in Sy.No.368 referred above has attained finality.
If the petitioner is aggrieved the compensation awarded in respect of the structures, the petitioner is at liberty to seek enhancement of compensation subject to the just exceptions under the law.

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 fairly submits that the award is not yet passed in respect of the land measuring 2428 square meters in the survey number referred above.
Since the award is already passed in respect of the structure over the land, considering the larger public purpose the award should be passed in respect of land.
Else the acquisition is complete only for the structure and the acquisition lapses for the land.

15. Under these circumstances, it is incumbent upon the first respondent-Authority to pass appropriate award in respect of the land referred above by following the provision of law which is applicable to determine the compensation in respect of the above said land.
16. For the reasons discussed, in the peculiar circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that the petitioner is not entitled to relief claimed in the present petition.

However, the petitioner is entitled to compensation in respect of the land referred above and the same shall be determined by the competent authority in accordance with the applicable provisions of law.
17. With these observations, the petition is disposed of.
18. It is made clear that the first respondent shall not delay the proceeding to determine the compensation in respect of the land in question which is acquired.
The whole exercise shall be completed within six months from today.
